title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror comes forward, Patrick Clancy speaks out | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Two weeks after the triple-murder trial of Lindsay Clancyended in a mistrial, new voices, including the lone holdout juror and Lindsay’s ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, are coming forward to speak out about the case.

The lone holdout juror in the trial – accused of having an “agenda” by Clancy’s defense attorney after the seven-week trial ended without a verdict – said in a statement Thursday his views on the Massachusetts mother were misrepresented by his fellow jurors.

“I didn’t have any doubts,” Michael Péguy Desronvil said in his statement. “As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence presented.”

The Boston Globe said this week it confirmed the identity of Desronvil, 48, through photos published online, court records and an interview with one of his fellow jurors.

The mistrial left Clancy’s future uncertain, as prosecutors have not yet decided whether to pursue a new trial.

In an extraordinary note to the judge on thesixth day of deliberations, the jury foreperson – later identified as Roni Carlson – said Desronvil “has made statements acknowledging doubt, but refuses to apply it to the verdict as the law states,” prompting anunsuccessful requestfrom Clancy’s defense attorney Kevin Reddington to have the juror replaced by an alternate.

But in his new statement, Desronvil says he felt all along the evidence pointed to a guilty verdict.

“Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses, and what the prosecution presented, I thought it was enough proof that she (Clancy) knew exactly what she was doing and planned,” he said in the statement.

The judge in the case declared a mistrial on September 4 after the jury repeatedly said it couldn’t reach a unanimous verdict. Clancy’s lawyer argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis when she killed her three children – Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months – at the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.

“There’s one juror who refuses to listen to the law that you’ve given him or her on reasonable doubt,” Reddingtontoldthe judge in his attempt to have the juror removed.

Since the mistrial was declared, several other jurors who were leaning toward findingClancy not guilty due to lack of criminal responsibility have given interviews describingfrustrating conversations inside the deliberation room.

“There was times he wouldn’t engage, like he’d be scrolling on his phone while people were talking to him, things like that,” juror Nick Dargie toldABC News.

“He had the hardest time getting off the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children,” juror Kellie Farina toldNBC10 Boston.

During the weekslong trial, Clancy acknowledged she killed her three children, but her lawyers argued she should not be held criminally responsible because she was in the midst of a psychotic episode when she fatally strangled them and attempted suicide.

The panel, comprised of nine women and three men, was unable to reach a unanimous verdict after more than 38 hours of deliberations. The jurors sent notes to the court indicating they were split 11 to 1, with the majority at one point alleging the lone holdout was unable to follow the law on reasonable doubt. The judge ultimately declared a mistrial.

Carlson toldNBC10there was no doubt Clancy killed her children, but said it was also obvious to jurors that she loved them.

The Plymouth County District Attorney’s Office previously declined to comment on reports about the juror identities. Clancy is due back in court for a hearing on September 29 as prosecutors determine whether to seek a retrial.

In astatement on X, lawyer Edward Andrew Paltzik said he was representing the holdout juror, writing “please pray for him and help us protect him,” without identifying the man.

“He is presently safe and sound at an undisclosed secure location in a rural area of Northern New England,” Paltzik wrote.

“Rest assured that the evil people who have so viciously attacked this American Hero and Champion of Justice will be held accountable to the maximum extent of the law and beyond,” the statement added, describing the man as a devoted father and man of God.

CNN has reached out to Paltzik for more information and whether any legal action is being taken on behalf of the juror.

“There will be a time for accountability and a time for the real story of the Lindsay Clancy Trial to be told. But not right now,”Paltzik said in a second post early Friday, adding neither he nor his client would be giving interviews.

“Any attempts to contact our Heroic Lone Holdout Juror will not be well-taken. Please respect his dignity, humanity, and privacy. Stay away from his home, stop calling him, and don’t even think about deciphering his location,” Paltzik wrote. “We look forward to sharing more information in the coming days on an appropriate timeline, including all of the ways in which you can support this incredible and unique man, and the cause of truth and justice that he so righteously stands for.”

“On behalf of our American Hero and Champion of Justice, thank you to all the patriotic Americans who have stood in solidarity behind him with such deeply touching generosity, kindness, and warmth,” he concluded.

Also coming forward following the end of the closely watched trial, is her ex-husband, Patrick Clancy. He and his new wife sat down for an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes,” which will air on Sunday.

Patrick Clancy had been the first witness called to testify in the triple-murder trial of his ex-wife.He spent two days testifying about Lindsay’s downward spiralthat culminated in the deaths of their three children.

In his interview,Clancy told CBS correspondent Ross Douthat he still talks to his kids “all the time.”

““What do you say?” Douthat asked. “Help me. All the time,” Clancy said. “Do they help you?” Douthat asked Clancy. “I like to believe they do. It’s a way I stay connected to them,” he replied.”

Asked by Douthat whether he feels angry at himself, Clancy said: “I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time, and I live with the outcome.”

“I live with it every day, but I think I did the best I could,” he repeated.

Dr. Rachel Danis, a fertility doctor in New York City, married Patrick Clancy in April, CBS reported. During the course of Lindsay’s trial, both Patrick and Danisbecame subjects of unfounded conspiracy theories.

Lawyers for Patrick recently announced they will take legal actionto stop the barrage of online conspiracy theorists.

Danis joined her husband for his interview with “60 Minutes.” “I don’t understand how this story has been so twisted,”she said in the interview. “But I would hope people know that Pat is, as I said before, the most selfless father and supportive partner, and I was just a girl that met a guy running in Central Park on a really cold Saturday, and I don’t think there’s anything wrong with that.”

CNN’s Eric Levenson, Cindy Von Quednow and Isa Mudannayake contributed to this report.

CNN’s Eric Levenson, Cindy Von Quednow and Isa Mudannayake contributed to this report.
